INTERVIEW STATEMENT - EMMIE MERCER

I see artificial intelligence as one of the most encouraging developments in education in years. Used thoughtfully, AI gives us another way to help students practice, ask questions, test ideas, and get unstuck when they are learning something difficult. I have been especially pleased to see students use AI to explain a technical concept in simpler language, brainstorm approaches to a project, or receive quick feedback before they bring a question to an instructor. Those uses can build confidence and make learning feel more accessible.

I am also excited by what AI can do for instructors. It can help us create examples, draft practice activities, compare different explanations, and spend less time on repetitive preparation. That does not mean the technology replaces good teaching. In my view, it gives a good instructor another useful tool. The best results happen when faculty stay involved, verify the output, and show students how to question what the system produces.

What I like most is the opportunity to teach responsible use instead of pretending students will never encounter these tools. Employers are already exploring AI, so our students should learn how to use it honestly and effectively. We should be very clear about when AI assistance is appropriate, how sources should be checked, and when students must demonstrate their own knowledge. Those expectations can coexist with experimentation.

Overall, I am optimistic. I have seen students become more curious and more willing to revise their work when AI is used as a tutor or brainstorming partner rather than as a shortcut. There will be mistakes and we will need sensible guidelines, but that is true of every new technology. I would much rather help students develop strong AI judgment now than send them into the workplace unprepared. For me, the possibilities are exciting, useful, and worth exploring.
